# ww3-gpu: rules that hold in every session and subagent

The full rulebook is `AGENTS.md` at the repository root; where this list and it differ,
`AGENTS.md` wins.

- **Write for scientists, carry evidence**: the first readers are PhD researchers, postdocs and
  independent researchers in wave modelling, numerical methods and HPC; every claim carries `(v)`
  with what was checked or `⚠` when it was not, and every number comes with the command that
  reproduces it (AGENTS.md, "Audience and evidence").
- **WW3 is read-only**: never vendor WW3 source or edit the Fortran physics; the `WW3/` and `WW3-noaa/` submodules
  and `$WW3` are references, and the only Fortran this repo adds is a shim behind a switch
  (AGENTS.md, "WW3 source").
- **No citation of a third party's issues**: an issue, pull request or discussion of a repository
  this project does not own (NOAA-EMC/WW3, NOAA-EMC/WW4, Kokkos, any other) is never cited,
  linked or named by its number in a file, commit, issue or pull request of this repository; a
  fact learned there is cited by what it describes, the code at a commit, a release or a published
  source (AGENTS.md, "Third-party issues").
- **Translate, don't improve**: a ported routine reproduces the Fortran's arithmetic; a change of
  reduction order, limiter or integration order is a separate PR with its own L2 evidence, asked
  about first, and a tolerance is never widened to pass (AGENTS.md, "Porting").
- **Bit for bit with the Fortran**: every ported routine gives the same bits as the Fortran
  routine it replaces, inside the same WW3 executable; `test.comp` finds no file different on any
  regtest entry that exercises it, and a tolerance is a diagnostic, never the verdict
  (AGENTS.md, "Bit for bit").
- **No full-spectrum copy to keep the copies in sync**: once `VA` is resident, no code path
  copies the whole spectrum between host and device per step, per grid or per `W3WAVE` call to
  keep the two copies consistent; a host write is followed by a sync of what it wrote, where it
  writes it (AGENTS.md, "Resident spectrum").
- **Speed is the goal, parity is its condition**: the repository exists to make WW3 run faster
  with Kokkos and CUDA without changing the Fortran's arithmetic; a speed figure carries the
  machine, the command and the median of three runs, and says "regtest pending ⚠" until WW3's
  regtests passed on its commit; the tables built from `bench/results/` still need that pass
  (ADR-0016).
- **The port has no tests of its own**: Kokkos code is validated only by WW3's regtests, run inside
  WW3 from the h0ffmann/WW3 fork and compared with the same WW3 without it; no L1, GoogleTest or
  fixture of a ported routine is written here
  (ADR-0010).
- **Regtests postponed to a validation phase**: WW3's regtests run when the owner calls the
  validation phase, which checks that the translation from Fortran to C++ was accurate; until
  then bit parity is argued statically (the `-O3` GIMPLE or disassembly of both compilers,
  `libm_bits` for device math), a row's `regtested` stays "no: postponed (ADR-0016)", and every
  flag defaults to the Fortran
  (ADR-0016, superseding
  ADR-0011).
- **Engineering work follows the compound loop**: when the owner asks for engineering work, plan,
  work, review and compound with Compound Engineering's skills, sized to the change, and redirect
  the steps that clash with these rules (AGENTS.md, "Engineering work").
- **The proposal goes through the reviewer**: any change under `pubs/proposal/` passes
  `revisor-proposta` and `just proposal-lint` before the PR, and the review is recorded
  (AGENTS.md, "The proposal").
- **Commits carry `Tested:`**, in the final block of the message, and never a `Cost:` trailer; an
  agent's branch is `goal/<id>-<slug>`, never `claude/…`; the PR is opened with `just pr`
  (AGENTS.md, "Commits and pull requests").

- **Never run `--ww3-gpu --gpu` without the owner supervising that run.** That is
  `scripts/ww3-gpu.sh --ww3-gpu <case> --gpu`, `just smoke-ww3-gpu gpu`, `just full-ww3-gpu gpu`,
  `just perf-ww3-gpu`, `just ww3-gpu-matrix-cuda` (the regtest matrix on Kokkos' CUDA backend) and
  their Docker forms (`just dsmoke-ww3-gpu gpu`, `just dfull-ww3-gpu gpu`, `just dperf-ww3-gpu`).
  The same holds for `scripts/libm_bits.sh --device`, which asks for the same "yes".
  `ww3-gpu.sh` and `scripts/gpu_supervised.sh` ask for a "yes" typed at a terminal and exit 7
  without one. Never work around it: no faked terminal, no `WW3GPU_IN_SHELL`, no
  `WW3GPU_GPU_CONFIRMED` (which the CUDA matrix's `setup:kokkos` and entries require), no piped
  answer. `--build-only` compiles for the GPU without running it and is allowed.
